summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain, left leg swelling, and dysuria. Evaluation revealed a new right bundle branch block on EKG, but serial troponins were stable and imaging ruled out pulmonary embolism, making acute coronary syndrome unlikely. The chest pain was attributed to worsening diastolic heart failure, supported by elevated BNP, cardiomegaly on imaging, and symptoms responsive to nitroglycerin. She was treated with IV and oral diuretics, with transition to 120 mg furosemide twice daily at discharge. During admission, she developed acute kidney injury, peaking at creatinine 4.2, which improved with diuresis and was attributed to pre-renal etiology. A urinary tract infection was confirmed with growth of Group B Strep and later Proteus mirabilis, prompting a switch to Augmentin. Her sternal wound cultured MRSA but showed no signs of infection; IV vancomycin was briefly given during a febrile episode but discontinued. Anemia was managed with one unit of packed red blood cells. Medications were adjusted, including reduction of metoprolol for bradycardia, increase in amlodipine, and addition of isosorbide mononitrate and gabapentin. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved symptoms, and follow-up planned with cardiology, nephrology, and urology.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
